article_content: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark 9.11.2023 The conflict between Israel and the terrorist organisation Hamas has led to a growing humanitarian catastrophe and protection crisis for civilians. Particularly in Gaza, there is an acute shortage of basic necessities, such as food, water, medicine, electricity, and fuel - and the impacts on children are especially severe. Denmark has therefore decided to increase its humanitarian aid to the Palestinian civilian population, particularly in Gaza, by 150 million Danish kroner (approx. 20 million euro). This new aid focuses on the protection of children, emergency aid, and food for the civilian population, the delivery of medicine and medical equipment, and medical treatment for the sick and injured. 'The humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic and worsening by the day - not least for the children. Therefore, the Government has decided to support the humanitarian efforts with an additional 150 million kroner (approx. 20 million euro). With this new humanitarian contribution, we are focusing on supporting efforts that can help the many children who are severely impacted. And there remains an urgent need to assist civilians with emergency humanitarian aid, access to clean water, and treatment of the sick and wounded. Denmark is also working with the EU and via other channels for improvements in unhindered humanitarian access to Gaza and is leading international efforts to negotiate a ceasefire, ensuring humanitarian pauses in the conflict so that emergency aid can enter and reach civilians,' says Minister for Development Cooperation and Global Climate Policy, Dan Jørgensen. Catastrophic consequences for the civilian population In Gaza, more than 10,000 civilians - including more than 4,000 children - have lost their lives since the beginning of the conflict on 7 October. An additional 1.5 million people have been displaced. Aid workers and hospitals are facing major challenges in their efforts to provide humanitarian aid and protection, including difficult conditions on the ground with ongoing military combat, depletion of storage capacities and fuel stocks, and continued challenges in getting sufficient emergency aid into Gaza. The new DKK 150 million (approx. EURO 20 million) humanitarian aid package will be distributed between the following organisations: UNICEF (DKK 60 million, approx. EURO 8 million): Focus on protection of children, access to clean water and hygiene. WFP (DKK 40 million, approx. EURO 5.4 million): Focus on food efforts and logistics. UNRWA (DKK 18 million, approx. EURO 2.4 million): Focus on protection of displaced persons, including children, and provision of basic emergency aid. ICRC (DKK 32 million, approx. EURO 4.2 million): Focus on the supply of medicine, medical equipment and medical treatment. The new aid will be announced in connection with the international humanitarian conference in Paris on 9 November, where Minister for Development Cooperation and Global Climate Policy, Dan Jørgensen, will be a participant. The aid package comes in addition to the Danish Government's previous announcement of extraordinary humanitarian aid to Palestine, and brings the total humanitarian contribution to Palestine since the beginning of the conflict on 7 October to DKK 250 million (approx. EURO 33.4 million).
translated_content: Ministri ng Ugnayan sa Labor ng Denmark 9.11.2023 Ang konflikto sa pagitan ng Israel at ng teroristang organisasyong Hamas ay nagdulot ng isang lumalaking krisis sa humanitaryo at proteksyon para sa mga sibilyan. Partikular sa Gaza, may malubhang kawalan ng mga pangunahing nekisidad tulad ng pagkain, tubig, gamot, kuryente, at langis - at ang epekto sa mga bata ay lalo ngang malubha. Dahil dito, nagpasya ang Denmark na dagdagan ang tulong sa humanitaryo para sa sibilyang populasyon ng Palestina, partikular sa Gaza, na nagkakahalagang 150 milyong kroner ng Denmark (humigit-kumulang 20 milyong euro). Ang tulong na ito ay nakatuon sa proteksyon ng mga bata, tulong sa emergency, at pagkain para sa mga sibilyan, paghahatid ng mga gamot at medikal na kagamitan, at medikal na pagtrato sa mga may sakit at sugatan. 'Ang situwasyon sa humanitaryo sa Gaza ay katastropiko at lumalala araw-araw - lalo na para sa mga bata. Kaya't nagpasya ang Gobyerno na suportahan ang mga pagsisikap na humanitaryo kasama ang dagdag na 150 milyong kroner (humigit-kumulang 20 milyong euro). Sa pamamagitan ng bagong tulong na ito, nilalayon nating tulungang malake ang maraming bata na labis na naapektuhan. At may dagdag pa ring kirot na pangangailangan upang tulungan ang mga sibilyan kasama ang tulong sa emergency, access sa malinis na tubig, at paggamot sa mga may sakit at sugatan. Ang Denmark ay nagtatrabaho rin kasama ang EU at sa pamamagitan ng iba pang mga channel para sa pagbuti ng walang-hadlang na access sa humanitaryong tulong sa Gaza at nagpapantas ng mga pagsisikap na humanitaryo at negosasyon para sa pagpuno ng digmaan upang ang mga tulong sa emergency ay makarating sa mga sibilyan,' ayon kay Minister para sa Development Cooperation at Global Climate Policy, Dan Jørgensen. Katastropikong epekto para sa populasyong sibilyan Sa Gaza, higit sa 10,000 na sibilyan - kasama ang higit sa 4,000 bata - ang nawalan ng buhay mula noong pagsisimula ng konflikto noong Oktubre 7. Dagdag pa, higit sa 1.5 milyong tao ang nawalan ng tirahan. Ang mga manggagawa sa tulong at ospital ay nagkakaroon ng malalaking hamon sa kanilang pagsisikap na bigyan ng tulong na humanitaryo at proteksyon, kasama ang mga hirap na kondisyon sa lupa may mga nagpapatuloy na labanan, pagubos ng mga stock ng imbakan at langis, at patuloy na mga hamon sa pagpapadala ng sapat na tulong sa emergency sa Gaza.

article_content: Tortoise Investment Management LLC drastically reduced its stake in Vanguard Intermediate-Term Corporate Bond ETF (NASDAQ:VCIT) by 86.0% in Q2 2023, Holdings Channel reports. The ETF aims to track the Barclays Capital U.S. 5-10 Year Corporate Bond Index, targeting U.S. corporate bonds within a 5-10 year maturity range.
